t.4.2.1: But on seeing those two great-souled brothers, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, heroes bearing excellent weapons, Sugrīva became apprehensive.
t.4.2.2: With an agitated heart, gazing about in all directions, the bull among monkeys could not remain still in any one place.
t.4.2.4: Having reflected and weighed what was weighty and what was slight, that righteous-souled Sugrīva, deeply agitated, was there together with all his followers.
t.4.2.5: Then Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, gazing at Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa and greatly alarmed, spoke to his ministers.
t.4.2.3: Gazing at those two of great strength, he could not set his mind at rest; the heart of the monkey who had drawn near sank utterly within him.
t.4.2.6: Surely these two have been sent by Vālin; clad in bark garments as a disguise, wandering about, they have come here to this impenetrable forest.
t.4.2.7: Then Sugrīva's ministers, having seen the two supreme archers, went from that mountain slope to another, loftier peak.
t.4.2.8: Then those monkeys, the leaders of the troops, quickly approached the bull among troop-leaders, the foremost of the vānaras, and surrounding him, they stood in attendance upon him.
t.4.2.9: Converging all together on a single spot, they leapt from mountain to mountain, and with their speed they shook the peaks of the mountains.
t.4.2.10: Then all the mighty monkeys, leaping about, broke the flowering trees that grew there in the inaccessible places.
t.4.2.11: Then the foremost of the monkeys went leaping all over that great mountain, terrifying the deer, wildcats and tigers.
t.4.2.12: Then the ministers of Sugrīva, who had taken refuge on that lord of mountains, all came together with the chief of the monkeys and stood with their palms joined in reverence.
t.4.2.13: Then Hanumān, skilled in speech, spoke these words to Sugrīva, who was stricken with fear and apprehensive of some treachery on the part of Vālin.
t.4.2.14: O bull among monkeys, I do not see here that cruel Vālin of cruel appearance, from whom you fled with a troubled mind.
t.4.2.15: O gentle one, the evil-minded Vālī, your elder brother of sinful deeds, from whom your fear arises, is not here; I see no danger for you.
t.4.2.16: Ah, your monkey nature is plainly evident, O monkey, since through fickleness of mind you cannot hold yourself steady in sound judgment.
t.4.2.18: Sugrīva, having heard all the auspicious words of Hanūmān, then spoke to Hanūmān words more auspicious still.
t.4.2.17: Endowed with intelligence and discernment, carry out everything by reading signs and gestures; for a king who has fallen into folly does not rule over all beings.
t.4.2.19: Who would not feel fear on seeing these two, long-armed and large-eyed, bearing arrows, bows and swords, resembling the sons of the gods?
t.4.2.20: I suspect that these two excellent men have been sent by Vālin, for kings have many friends, and trust is not fitting here.
t.4.2.21: Enemies who move about in disguise must be recognized by a man, for they, untrusting themselves, strike at the weak points of those who trust.
t.4.2.22: O far-seeing kings, Vālī is shrewd in his undertakings. Such men become slayers of their foes, and they are to be found out through ordinary men.
t.4.2.24: Discern their disposition, whether they are glad at heart, winning their trust again and again with words of praise and with friendly gestures.
t.4.2.23: Going there in the guise of an ordinary person, O monkey, you must find out about those two through the nature of their gestures, and through their appearance and their speech.
t.4.2.26: O monkey, find out whether these two are pure of heart; their wickedness, if any, is to be discerned either from their speech or from their appearance.
t.4.2.25: Standing face to face with them on my behalf, O bull among monkeys, ask those two bow-bearers the purpose of their entering this forest.
t.4.2.27: Thus instructed by the king of the monkeys, the son of the Wind resolved to go to where those two, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, were.
t.4.2.28: Saying "So be it," and honouring the words of that greatly frightened yet unassailable monkey, the magnanimous Hanumān then went to where Rāma and the exceedingly mighty Lakṣmaṇa were.
